# 02 Default control bar, onStepChange, and the controls override seam

## Outcome

A board created with default options now shows a floating Prev/Next/Reset control bar positioned
relative to its own container, wired to `board.controller`. Consumers can turn it off or replace
it entirely, and can observe every step change (whether triggered by the built-in buttons or by
calling `board.controller` directly) via `onStepChange`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] By default (`options.controls` omitted or `true`), `createBoard` renders a Prev/Next/Reset
      control bar inside the container, `position: absolute` (or equivalent) relative to the
      container — not `position: fixed` to the viewport — so two boards on one page, or a board
      embedded in a card/sidebar, each keep their own bar next to their own canvas.
- [ ] The bar's buttons call `board.controller.next()` / `.prev()` / `.reset()`.
- [ ] `options.controls: false` renders no control bar at all.
- [ ] `options.controls: (board) => ({ element, destroy? })` renders the factory's `element`
      instead of the built-in bar; `destroy` (if provided) is called when `board.destroy()` runs.
- [ ] `options.onStepChange(current, total)` fires once per step change, regardless of whether the
      change came from the built-in buttons or from a consumer calling
      `board.controller.next()/prev()/reset()` directly (e.g. from a custom `ControlsFactory`).
- [ ] `onStepChange` does not fire on construction unless a `source` was provided and produced a
      non-empty timeline (i.e. it only fires on an actual step change, not a synthetic initial
      call with `(0, 0)` for a source with no timeline).
- [ ] The built-in bar's DOM carries stable, documented CSS class names so a consumer can restyle
      it from their own stylesheet without using `options.controls`.
- [ ] `board.destroy()` removes the control bar's DOM and its event listeners along with the rest
      of the instance.

## Test seam

Same as ticket 01: `createBoard`/`Board`, integration tests under jsdom. New assertions cover
button click → controller state change → `onStepChange` invocation, the `controls: false` and
`controls: <factory>` paths, and that a controller call made without touching the buttons still
fires `onStepChange`.
